question: Owner iMessage Oct 24 9:47 PM CT (phonemsg-01M5RF95KX989T909SG99JJ9F7): "I think this is the models first big win. How can we learn from this" - winning 4-leg Kansas/ASU/Arkansas State/Wisconsin ML receipt.

ticket_facts.receipt: FanDuel TN, placed Oct 24 10:20 AM CT, $10 stake, 4 moneyline legs: Kansas +103, Arizona State +107, Arkansas State +129, Wisconsin +140. Combined +1720 boosted to +2235 by a 30% profit boost. Won $233.56 ($223.56 profit).
ticket_facts.boost_separated: At the unboosted +1720 the same $10 returns $182.00 ($172.00 profit). The 30% boost added $51.56 - 23.1% of the actual profit came from the promotion, not the picks. Tracker records net against the actual receipt; model learning uses only the 4 winner picks, never the payout.
ticket_facts.note: Owner variant of the published research long shot (IL morning capture had Kansas -110, ASU -108, ArkSt +116, Wisconsin +126); receipt prices govern for money, and all four receipt legs were plus-money underdogs.

what_the_model_did.line_context: By ESPN/DraftKings closing lines (comparison only), 3 of the 4 legs closed as underdogs; Kansas closed a pick'em/slight favorite - the +103 on the receipt was a morning TN price. All four were sealed outright model picks published before kickoff.
what_the_model_did.slate_context: Saturday CT slate: no-AP reference 33/44 winners (75.0%). Full Week 8 holdout: 40/56 (71.4%, CI95 [58.9, 82.1]), MAE 10.79.

the_misses.three_leg_model_favorite: Went 2/3: Texas A&M +13.5 covered (Bama won by 11), Wisconsin +2.5 won outright, Clemson -2.5 missed - model had Clemson by 10.4 and Clemson lost by 4 (14.4-pt error, the model's worst same-direction favorite call of the day).
the_misses.tennessee: Tennessee at South Carolina was correctly left OFF both tickets: model SC by 0.9 vs book SC -2.5, only a 1.6-pt gap, below the edge bar. Model still had SC right (won 27-24) - the discipline was in not forcing a small gap into a leg.

signal_vs_luck.pattern: "Model picks a book underdog to win outright" - the pattern behind the winning ticket. Dog classification uses ESPN/DraftKings closing lines (comparison only; receipt legs were FanDuel TN morning prices).
signal_vs_luck.derivation_week: Week 8: model dog picks went 6/8 (75.0%) while all book dogs went 19/55 (34.5%). Binomial tail vs the dog base rate: p=0.024 - but this is the week the pattern was noticed on, so it cannot validate itself.
signal_vs_luck.unseen_test: Week 7 (unseen for this pattern, same repaired model lineage): model dog picks went 6/11 (54.5%) vs all dogs 20/59 (33.9%); binomial tail p=0.131 - above baseline but inside luck at this sample.
signal_vs_luck.combined_descriptive: 12/19 (63.2%) vs 39/114 (34.2%), p=0.009 - descriptive only; combining the derivation week inflates it.
signal_vs_luck.verdict: Promising, not proven. The unseen week points the same direction but does not clear a significance bar. No new betting signal is adopted; the winner-first sealed gates still govern any model change, and nothing about the model changes on one week.

what_changes.model: Nothing. No AP adoption (Week 8 gate failed again: paired winner CI95 [-0.054, 0.000]); no refit or retuning against Week 8 outcomes; no promotion on one week.
process: Keep publishing fragile-call flags - the two sub-point legs (Kansas 0.59, ASU 0.21) were flagged before kickoff, and that honesty is what makes the wins interpretable.
Boost math stays separated from pick quality in the tracker (23.1% of this profit was the promotion).
Predeclared prospective tracking: log every model dog-pick each week with its closing-line reference and grade the bucket after each week, rather than re-measuring on the week that suggested it.
Small-gap discipline (the Tennessee exclusion) stays the rule: a model lean under the edge bar is not a leg.

limits: Dog/favorite reference is ESPN/DraftKings closing lines, not the owner's FanDuel TN prices; closing vs morning movement matters (Kansas).
The model has no injury adjustment and the weather candidate failed validation.
Week 8 is the second graded holdout week; both the 71.4% winner rate and the dog-bucket edge rest on small samples.
